status: Historical precedents and proposed game abstractions; no runtime changes
method: A documented agreement is evidence for a subject and partner, not evidence that a proposed party government signed it. Earlier adoption of a later precedent is explicitly alternate history. Numerical rewards are balance proposals.

sources.title: ICPR: history and conventions
sources.supports: Commission founded in 1950; chemical-pollution and chloride conventions signed in 1976. Supports water monitoring and infrastructure cooperation; no native pollution simulation is claimed.

sources.title: Bonn Agreement: history
sources.supports: 1969 marine-pollution agreement, signatories including France, Britain and Norway, requested mutual assistance, research and exercises; 1977 Ekofisk and 1978 Amoco Cadiz illustrate operational pressures.

sources.title: French law approving the Franco-Swiss disaster-assistance agreement
sources.supports: Agreement signed in Bern on14 January1987; parliamentary approval30 December1988. Earlier adoption by an alternate government is a proposal, not a1970 historical fact.

sources.title: Council of Europe: transfrontier cooperation convention ETS106
sources.supports: Opened21 May1980; cross-border local-authority cooperation provides a later institutional precedent, not a mandatory date or automatic Community membership for bilateral technical offers.

sources.title: INA: René Dumont's official1974 campaign broadcast
sources.supports: The1974 broadcast made water scarcity and waste central ecological concerns. A1970 ecology-led government and its detailed armed-force institutions are counterfactual.

sources.title: Contemporary report of CID/UNATI demands,11 March1970
sources.supports: Nicoud's constituency protested taxes, health-insurance charges and large-store competition; demanded an independent craft/commerce bank. Proposed foreign credit or military workshop contracts are extrapolation, not a CID platform.

sources.title: Larousse: CIDUNATI institutional history
sources.supports: CID/UNATI represented artisans and independent traders, with protest and later professional electoral participation. It must not be confused with CNI.

sources.title: Contemporary report of the FN1973 programme
sources.supports: Programme discussed European confederation and priority defence coordination with Britain. This differs from projecting the contemporary RN's policy backward.

sources.title: Vie publique: Le Pen's1988 defence statement
sources.supports: Later proposals included armament standardisation and Franco-British/Franco-German defence coordination, increased spending and national-service reform. A different governing choice can prioritise national suppliers. No treaty, foreign command or weapons programme is automatically enacted.

sources.title: Dassault: Greece and its aircraft relationship
sources.supports: Greece ordered Mirage F1 aircraft in1974 and Mirage2000 in1985. Recurring reciprocal supplier/maintenance conventions are proposed extensions; no aircraft or free technology is delivered.

sources.title: Dassault: Alpha Jet origins and production
sources.supports: Franco-German joint programme, differing1971 requirements, first flight1973, French operational service1979. Supports production workshare, training and the risk of diverging requirements.

sources.title: Dassault: Jaguar origins and production
sources.supports: 1965 Anglo-French cooperative agreement,1968 orders and first flight, two assembly lines, changing requirements and rising cost. Supports both cooperation benefits and programme tradeoffs.

sources.title: CNES: origins of Franco-Soviet human-spaceflight cooperation
sources.supports: 1966 science agreement,1979 invitation,1980 selection and1982 French flight. Proposed exchanges are peaceful instrumentation, not automatic strategic project completion.

sources.title: Dacia: official industrial history
sources.supports: 1966 Renault licensing contract,1968 assembly and1969 Renault12-based Dacia1300; later negotiations failed. Civil vehicle licensing is documented; military utility tooling is an explicit dual-use extrapolation.

sources.title: Mitterrand's1982 explanation of Algerian gas co-development
sources.supports: Supply costs, LNG transport and the public co-development contribution were contested. Efficiency/training spirits abstract industrial cooperation without adding free gas or silently creating a trade contract.

sources.title: Senate1983 budget report: Algeria and the gas contract
sources.supports: Discusses3 February1982 contract and its public budget consequences. Monetary amounts in the proposal are game-balance costs, not unconverted francs from the report.

sources.title: Senate1983 report on announced army reorganisation
sources.supports: A rapid-action command and force of five divisions was planned as part of1984–1988 reorganisation; implementation phased from1984. A socialist rapid-response branch can be a documented later governing direction, or an earlier RP proposal, not a force granted in1970.

sources.title: National Assembly: Michel Debré's parliamentary interventions
sources.supports: 1969–1971 debates link independent deterrence, territorial defence, conscription, intervention, procurement cost and industry. Scarce-budget emphasis is an interpretation; deterrence and conventional forces were not absolute historical opposites.

root_conclusions.ecology: Use water, electricity conservation, repair, rescue and defensive engineering. Different priorities inside a counterfactual government; no automatic nuclear disarmament.
root_conclusions.cid: Credit/repair institutions versus small-supplier output represent different constraints of the same historical trader constituency. No documented CID defence or foreign platform is invented.
root_conclusions.national: Keep the historical1972 founding gate and distinguish1973 European-confederation rhetoric from later1988 policy. Both national-supplier and intergovernmental cooperation routes are proposed governing allocations.
root_conclusions.invariants: No forced foreign acceptance, regime, war, alliance, access, nuclear sharing or technology unlock. Partner offers have concrete consent-stage costs and modest continuing gains plus continuing disadvantages.
root_conclusions.tags: Active project tags verified: GER for West Germany, DDR for East Germany, SER for1970 Yugoslavia, HOL for Netherlands, NRY for Norway, GRE for Greece, SWI for Switzerland. Vanilla WGR/YUG/NOR are not assumed.
